derivations.claim: Since $d$ is the finite VC dimension, choose distinct $x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_{d-1}$ shattered by $\mathcal H$. For each of the finitely many label vectors $\theta\in\{0,1\}^d$, shattering supplies a target $f_\theta\in\mathcal H$ with those labels on these points; finite choice suffices for this finite family. Put $\epsilon=(d-1)/(32m)$ and define the finite mixture $\mu=(1-8\epsilon)\delta_{x_0}+\sum_{i=1}^{d-1}\frac{8\epsilon}{d-1}\delta_{x_i}$. The range on $m$ gives $8\epsilon=(d-1)/(4m)\le1$, so all mixture weights are nonnegative and sum to one. For each $\theta$, let $D_\theta$ be the law of $(X,f_\theta(X))$ for $X\sim\mu$.

Let $M$ count sample positions drawn from the rare atoms $x_1,\ldots,x_{d-1}$. Then $M\sim\operatorname{Bin}(m,8\epsilon)$ and $\mu_0:=\mathbb EM=(d-1)/4\ge1/4$. Since $e^p=\sum_{j=0}^\infty p^j/j!\ge1+p$ for $p\ge0$, $\mathbb E2^M=(1+8\epsilon)^m\le e^{\mu_0}$. For any nonnegative random variable $X$ and $b>0$, $\mathbb EX\ge b\Pr\{X\ge b\}$ because $X\ge b\mathbf1_{\{X\ge b\}}$; apply this to $X=2^M$ and $b=2^{2\mu_0}$. On $\{M\ge2\mu_0\}$, $2^M\ge2^{2\mu_0}$, hence $\Pr\{M\ge2\mu_0\}\le e^{\mu_0-2\mu_0\log2}\le e^{-\mu_0/3}$, where $\log2\ge2/3$ because $g(x)=\log x-2(x-1)/(x+1)$ has $g(1)=0$ and $g'(x)=(x-1)^2/(x(x+1)^2)\ge0$ for $x\ge1$. Since $2\mu_0=(d-1)/2$, $\Pr\{M\le(d-1)/2\}\ge1-e^{-\mu_0/3}\ge1-e^{-1/12}\ge1/13$; the last inequality follows from $e^{1/12}\ge1+1/12=13/12$.

Fix any vector of sample atom indices and observed labels for which $M\le(d-1)/2$. At least $(d-1)/2$ rare atoms were not observed. Under the uniform prior on $\theta$, each unseen label $\theta_i$ is still an independent fair bit, independent of the learner's output at $x_i$, because the learner depends only on the observed sample and independent internal randomness. Therefore, if $W$ is the learner's risk contribution from $x_1,\ldots,x_{d-1}$, then $\mathbb E_{\theta,A}[W\mid\text{observed data}]\ge\frac12\frac{d-1}{2}\frac{8\epsilon}{d-1}=2\epsilon$, while $0\le W\le8\epsilon$. Applying [F2] to $W/(8\epsilon)$ at $t=1/8$ yields $\Pr_{\theta,A}\{W>\epsilon\mid\text{observed data}\}\ge1/7$.

Each $D_\theta$ is realizable by $f_\theta$, so [F4] gives $R_{D_\theta}^*(\mathcal H)=0$. By [F3] and the event $Y=f_\theta(X)$ of probability one, the zero-one risk and target risk of the learner's output agree. The full target risk is at least $W$. Averaging step 1.3 over sample locations and labels, then using step 1.2, gives $\Pr_{\theta,S\sim D_\theta^m,A}\{R_{D_\theta}(A(S),f_\theta)>\epsilon\}\ge\frac1{7}\cdot\frac1{13}=\frac1{91}>\frac1{100}$. This is an average over the finite set $\{0,1\}^d$, so at least one $\theta$ has conditional failure probability at least $1/91$. Its $D_\theta$ and $f_\theta$ satisfy the statement.
